Topics
Codex as an agentic software engineer
Codex versus traditional coding assistants
Codex development surfaces:

o Cloud workflows
o GitHub workflows
o Non-interactive execution
o SDK and App Server
The Codex execution loop:
o Understand
o Inspect

o Execute
o Validate

o Report
Repository context versus conversation context

o Diagnose

Engineering Principle
Codex should not start by writing code. A professional workflow starts with:
1. Understanding the repository.
2. Establishing the baseline.
3. Identifying evidence.
4. Confirming scope.
5. Defining success.
6. Only then implementing changes.

Lab 3: Repository Engineering Constitution
Required rules:
Payment changes require idempotency tests.
Database changes require rollback instructions.
Public API changes require compatibility review.
New external calls require timeout and retry policies.
Sensitive data must not be logged.
Infrastructure changes require security validation.
Every defect fix requires a regression test.
Final reports must include commands executed and results.
Lab Deliverable
A tested instruction hierarchy showing that Codex applies different guidance to backend, frontend and
infrastructure components.

subtopics: Separating root causes from secondary symptoms
modules.reference_text:
Professional Implementation Workflow
1. Inspect the issue.
2. Establish a clean baseline.
3. Reproduce the problem.
4. Identify the failing code path.
5. Form a root-cause hypothesis.
6. Verify the hypothesis.
7. Add a failing regression test.
8. Implement the smallest safe patch.
9. Run focused tests.
10. Run broader regression tests.
11. Review the final diff.
12. Document evidence and remaining risks.

Lab 6: Create Secure Operating Profiles
Participants design:
repo-analyst – Architecture and investigation – Read-only
developer – Code modification and testing – Workspace write
security-reviewer – Adversarial code review – Read-only
ci-reviewer – Non-interactive PR analysis – Read-only, no approvals
isolated-remediator – Controlled patch creation – Workspace write in isolated runner
Lab Test
Participants verify that:
The analyst cannot modify files.
The developer can edit only approved workspace files.
Network operations require the expected authorization.
Unapproved destructive operations fail.
CI operation does not pause waiting for a person.

modules.reference_text:
Scenario
The payment router receives 12,000 requests per second, while a destination bank safely handles only 4,000
requests per second.
Observed Symptoms
Bank latency rises sharply.
Timeout rate reaches 20%.
Retried requests increase incoming load.
Database connections saturate.
Kafka lag grows.
Redis in-flight counters become inconsistent.
Duplicate-payment risk appears.
Logs expose sensitive identifiers.
Alerts do not identify the actual bottleneck.
Participant Tasks
Retrieve incident information through MCP.
Map the complete request path.
Identify amplification caused by retries.
Examine timeout and circuit-breaker behaviour.
Analyse Redis, database and Kafka usage.
Reproduce the failure under controlled load.
Propose rate limiting and backpressure.
Protect payment idempotency.
Improve metrics and logs.
Implement one minimal safe correction.
Add regression and fault-injection tests.
Produce a rollback plan.
Day 2 Assessment
Participants defend their solution against cross-questions from:
Application engineering
SRE
Security
Database engineering
Business operations
Day 3 – Automation, SDK, Evaluation and Enterprise Deployment
